**Found the real shape of the gap.** The zone's own `sustain` text genuinely answers this question ("a shelf life the pack does not print, because your baby grows while the packs sit still"), rendered in full on the page body, but `ops/build_zone_pages.py`'s `zone_faq()`, the function that turns page content into FAQPage headings and structured data, only ever builds questions from five fixed fields (`session`, `done_looks_like`, `the_call`, `leave_behind`, `shine_detail`, `watch_for`) and `sustain` is not one of them, by its own docstring's design. So no zone's `sustain` text can ever reach a heading, and this class of query ("how long does X last," "how do you know when to restock X") can never score above a coincidental tie anywhere on the site, however directly the real content answers it.

**Checked whether this reaches beyond Nursery, and caught my own false positive before writing it down as a finding.** A first keyword grep for durability language across all 20 rooms' `sustain` text returned 4 hits; reading each in context, not just counting them, showed 3 of the 4 are coincidental substring matches whose actual claim is the opposite of durability (Pantry: cans "never force the issue by spoiling"; Mudroom: wet shoes "never expire on its own"; Home Office: no real "use by" phrase present, a cross-word accident). Only Nursery's match is genuine. The mechanism gap is confirmed real; its reach beyond Nursery is not, and is not asserted.

**Deliberately not built this cycle.** A new `zone_faq()` question sourced from `sustain` would touch all 114 zones' FAQPage structured data at once, and this sandbox's `gate_tests` cannot run to completion (the documented headless-Chromium/no-egress hang), so there is no way to fail-then-pass a schema-surface change like this against the full suite before shipping, the bar every other structured-data fix this week was held to. Shipping it unverified on a surface search engines parse directly would be a worse outcome than leaving one query unrouted. Recorded as `BACKLOG-2026-09-07.md` entry 135 for whichever cycle next has the hours this needs, rather than forced into this slot.

An earlier attempt this same cycle to drop every page's promotional cross-sell "band" section wholesale was tried against a full-corpus diff and reverted: that class of heading varies per room and often carries real zone-naming signal, unlike this one, which reads identically everywhere.

**Verified:** Added a regression test (`ops/tests/test_keyword_demand.py` case 21, a throwaway site tree) proving the filter keeps real title words while dropping the boilerplate; fail-then-pass proved directly, 26/26. `keyword_demand.py`/`keyword_demand_global.py --rescore`: both target queries moved to covered; the scorer fix also corrected several other previously-invisible false `covered` claims riding the same free "cleaning" word (a kitchen-properly query, six car/garage cleaning-supplies queries, two more), several now correctly redirected to Hall Closet's Cleaning Supply Zone instead of Garage; two diaper-disposal queries dropped from an undeserved `partial` to an honest `gap`, confirmed against the Nursery Changing Station's real headings, which never use the word "dispose". `check_also_called_digital_collision_fast.py`, `test_gate_also_called_no_digital_collision.py` (5/5), `test_gate_zone_also_called_is_heading.py` (6/6), `test_room_also_called.py` clean. `room_guide_underperformance.py --room "Home Office"`: 38% to 35% uncovered. `check_urls.py` (235/235), `audit_pages.py` (240/0), `fix_dashes.py`/`fix_dialect.py --check` (0/0), `affiliate.py --check` (165 documents), `link_graph_report.py` (0 orphans), `check_sellable.py` (124/126) all clean. `preflight.py --skip-tests` run fresh after, unbuffered to a file: 0 FAIL through every gate reached, genuinely stalled at the documented network-bound Stripe/GitHub-Actions gates (no `.env.secrets`), same standing sandbox limitation as every recent cycle.

**Went well:** running the full-corpus before/after diff instead of trusting a clean collision-checker run caught a real false "covered" claim before it shipped; following the cause instead of reverting turned one near-miss into a corpus-wide correction affecting more than a dozen queries.

**Did not go well:** the band-heading experiment tried and reverted this same cycle cost real time on a dead end; the lesson worth keeping is that a heading's wording VARYING per page is what makes it risky to touch, not whether it sits inside a promotional section.

**Changing next cycle:** `BOILERPLATE_HEADINGS` and its regression test are the gate this lesson earns. Other zone-template headings are also verified byte-identical corpus-wide ("Related reading", "Common items here" and others) but left alone until a second real collision is found, per CLAUDE.md's preference for a small reversible change over a speculative broad one.

## Scheduled operator cycle, 2026-11-05 (~05:0x UTC): fixed the root cause behind most of the last two weeks' one-at-a-time "zone misattribution" fixes

**Did:** Attached per Step 0 (fetch, real unshallow, `checkout -B main origin/main`, ff-only onto `316ba5093`, tree clean). Read `GOALS.md`, `BACKLOG-2026-09-07.md` sections 0 and 5-7, `STATUS.md`'s Open claims and Current Highest-Level Priority, `CLAUDE.md`, this file's last several entries, and GitHub directly (29 open issues, all `decision`/`blocked-on-art`, none from Phil, confirmed via the API not cited). `inbox_agent.py --apply`: no mail credential, standing gap, unchecked. Every one of the 29 issues is a genuine owner gate (money, accounts, art); none unblocked.

Before mining another single-word synonym (the dominant shape of work since 2026-10-21), checked a hunch instead of trusting the next room on `room_guide_underperformance.py`'s list: Stair Landing's two remaining partial rows ("way", "walk", both either a stopword or a likely autocomplete typo for "wall") and Pantry's 27 partial rows (mostly "ikea"/"pinterest"/"amazon"/"deep"/"wire", none a real zone synonym this content could honestly add) both confirmed genuinely exhausted, not reopened.

**Mining a different question instead of the same one again paid off.** Investigated why "master bedroom storage" was still scoring to a Kids Bedroom zone despite `ops/room-also-called.json` recording "master bedroom" as a measured synonym for Primary Bedroom since 2026-10-02 (`"covered": 0`), and despite `/rooms/primary-bedroom.html` already carrying the "Also called the master bedroom" heading. Traced it to `ops/keyword_demand.py`'s `score_rows()`: `best_page`/`best_page_title` were always set from the title-surface winner, even on rows where `matched_on` already recorded that the heading surface scored higher (or tied) and a different page earned the status. Checked the scope directly against the live corpus before writing a line of fix: 1402 of 2823 rows disagreed between the title-surface and heading-surface winner, 778 of those in a different ROOM entirely ("back porch careers" credited an unrelated article, "why your family won't put things back", instead of the Patio or Deck deck; "baby diaper caddy organizer" credited a baby-clothes article instead of the Nursery's own diaper zone; and so on). `room_guide_candidates.py` and `room_guide_underperformance.py` both read `best_page` as "the page this query actually routes to" by design (their own docstrings say so), so every one of those 778 was a live risk of a future cycle "fixing" a misattribution by adding a dishonest also-called label to the wrong zone, exactly the failure mode CLAUDE.md's affiliate/testimonial honesty rules exist to catch in a different place.

**Fixed at the root, not the symptom.** `score_rows()` now decides one winning surface (title or heading) before using it anywhere downstream, and breaks an exact tie between the two surfaces the same way `_tie_break()` already breaks a tie within one surface: the page matching the query's own room signal wins, not whichever surface happens to run first in the code. `keyword_demand_global.py` reuses `keyword_demand.py`'s functions directly, so one fix covers both the US and global corpora with no duplicate change needed.

**Verified:** Two new numbered cases in `ops/tests/test_keyword_demand.py` (case 20a: a clean heading win pointing at a different page than the title winner; case 20b: an exact cross-room tie, the real "master bedroom storage" shape, plus a same-tie-no-signal regression check). Fail-then-pass proved directly: `git stash` on `ops/keyword_demand.py` alone, reran the test, watched both new assertions fail with the exact wrong URLs the live bug produced, `git stash pop`, reran, both passed. `python ops/keyword_demand.py --rescore` and `python ops/keyword_demand_global.py --rescore`: gap/partial/covered totals unchanged (112/1262/1449 US, 97/931/1142 global), exactly as expected since the fix corrects attribution, not scores. Spot-checked the regenerated `ops/KEYWORD-DEMAND.md` by eye: "back porch careers" now points at the Patio or Deck deck, not the unrelated article. Re-ran `check_also_called_digital_collision_fast.py`, `test_gate_zone_also_called_is_heading.py` (6/6), `test_gate_also_called_no_digital_collision.py` (5/5), `test_room_also_called.py`, and the four `keyword-demand*-rescored-current`/`not-stale` gate tests: all still pass. Full `preflight.py --skip-tests` run to completion afterward (written unbuffered to a file rather than piped through `tail`, the buffering trap several prior entries have logged): every gate passed, 39 warnings, all standing sandbox gaps (no Stripe/SSH/mail credential, Etsy fee page 403, screen-reader untested), 0 FAIL.

**Went well:** checking why an already-measured, already-rendered synonym still was not working, instead of accepting "covered: 0, needs a content fix" at face value, found a tooling bug with 778 room-level misattributions behind it instead of one more content gap.

**Did not go well:** this bug has been live since the heading-surface scoring pass shipped 2026-10-01, over a month, during which at least some of the one-at-a-time misattribution fixes this log already recorded (pegboard, chargers, hutch, bedside table, hallway closet) may have been chasing symptoms that this fix would have prevented from being symptoms at all. Not re-auditing each of those individually this cycle: they were each independently verified honest against real zone content at the time, so none are now known wrong, only possibly redundant.

**Changing next cycle:** none beyond the fix itself; `_tie_break`'s room-signal preference is now the single place this kind of tie gets decided, surface or no surface, so this class of bug should not recur in a new shape.

**Next:** re-run `room_guide_underperformance.py` across all 20 rooms with the corrected attribution before resuming the synonym-mining lane; several rooms' partial/gap lists will have shifted (some rows that looked like a gap in the wrong room will disappear, some real gaps in the right room may now be visible for the first time). Nothing from the 29 open issues is unblocked; no reply from Phil.

No content, price or product page touched; this is a measurement-tool fix, not a site change, so IndexNow is not applicable. Dashboard regenerated. Pushed to main.

**The 17:1x cycle's "fixed" dashboard commit count broke again 6 minutes after it shipped, and this time the actual mechanism was found, not just re-patched.** `EXECUTIVE-DASHBOARD-LIVE.md`'s "Commits (7 days)" row read "unknown (shallow clone, could not verify)" again at the top of this cycle, even though `dashboard.py` already tries a best-effort `git fetch --unshallow` before counting. Traced it instead of re-running the generator a third time and calling it done: `fc39628f2` ("Hourly check-in record", 17:27Z, the `hourly-brief.yml` GitHub Actions workflow) had overwritten the 17:1x fix with "unknown" again. That workflow's own `dashboard.py` call runs inside `sh()`'s shared 60-second subprocess timeout, and `git count-objects -v` shows this repository's pack is ~2.1GB, enough that an unshallow fetch does not reliably finish in 60s on every run, win some, lose some, which exactly matches the flapping between real numbers and "unknown" across recent cycles' dashboard diffs. This was never a bug in reporting "unknown" honestly (that behavior is correct and already tested, `ops/tests/test_send_brief_commits_7d.py`); the bug was a shared timeout too tight for this one call's real data volume.

**Fixed in `ops/dashboard.py`:** gave `sh()` an optional `timeout` parameter (default unchanged at 60s, so every other call is unaffected) and raised only the unshallow call to 240s, with a dated comment explaining why. Verified: `python3 -c "import ast; ast.parse(open('ops/dashboard.py').read())"` clean; `python3 ops/tests/test_send_brief_commits_7d.py` and `python3 ops/tests/test_last_commit_epoch_shallow_boundary.py` both `ok`, unaffected by the change; re-ran `ops/dashboard.py` from this session's own already-unshallowed tree and it reported real figures (`commits7d 1424` of 10720 total), not the fallback string. `fix_dashes.py --check` 0/0, `check_urls.py` 235/235 on the regenerated files.

**Not a guarantee the hourly job will now always get a real number** (a sufficiently slow or congested run could still exceed 240s), but 240s is four times the old budget against the same ~2.1GB pack, and the job's own `timeout-minutes: 20` leaves ample room for it. If this still flaps after this fix, the next real fix is on the workflow side (a non-zero `fetch-depth` on the `actions/checkout` step, or running the unshallow as its own step with its own timeout), not another bump to this number.

## Correction, same cycle, before handoff: the "0 FAIL" the 19:4x entry below reported was written before the run actually finished; the run then found a real-looking FAIL that turned out to be caused by this cycle's own still-shallow attach, and the root cause is fixed now

The 19:4x entry below pushed claiming "0 FAIL through every gate reached" while `preflight.py --skip-tests` was still running in the background. It went on to finish after that push and surfaced `FAIL epub-edition-date-current`: `build_epub.py`'s `EDITION_DATE` (2026-10-02) reading as older than `content/book/`'s own "last real commit," which it read as 2026-11-03.

**Checked before believing it, per CLAUDE.md 0.3/0.4.** `git log -1 -- content/book/` landed on `b7682ed1`, which `cat .git/shallow` confirmed was still a shallow boundary commit at that moment (this cycle's own `git fetch --unshallow` had silently stopped partway, the first attempt, the one the 19:4x entry watched by CPU and assumed was still progressing toward a real finish). A boundary commit has no visible parent locally, so `git log -1 -- path` cannot diff it against anything and treats it as having added every path in its own tree, including `content/book/`, which is why it read back with that commit's own date instead of the path's real last-touch date. Reran `git fetch --unshallow`; it completed this time (`is-shallow-repository` now `false`, 10,491 commits reachable). `git log -1 -- content/book/` then correctly resolved to `bf7fae4ede`, 2026-10-01 (2026-10-02 UTC, the exact day-boundary case `EDITION_DATE`'s own comment already documents), matching the constant exactly. Re-ran `gate_epub_edition_date_current()` directly: clean, no FAIL, no WARN. The FAIL was real output, not a flake, but the thing it was measuring was wrong, not the EPUB.

**Fixed the actual defect, not just this one FAIL.** `_last_commit_epoch()` (`ops/preflight.py`, also used by `gate_cover_author_current`, `gate_icons_current` and `gate_store_art`) had no guard against landing on a shallow boundary commit, unlike the precedent `gate_dashboard_shallow_commits` already set for the exact same failure direction (6.13: a plausible wrong value standing in for one never actually measured). Added a check against `.git/shallow`'s own contents: a result that lands on a recorded boundary commit now returns `None` ("could not measure") instead of that commit's own date, and every existing caller already treats `None` as "skip this check" rather than a false pass or fail. New test `ops/tests/test_last_commit_epoch_shallow_boundary.py`, three cases (a path really last touched before the boundary, a path genuinely touched by the boundary commit itself which still can't be told apart locally, and the real date still coming back once the boundary marker is gone), fail-then-pass proved by reverting the fix and re-running (`git stash`/`stash pop`), the same discipline the mcp-corpus test above it in the file follows.

**Verified.** `fix_dashes.py --check` 0/0. `cold_read_ledger.py --stale` 0 (nothing to compare against yet since this commit had not landed). The real `gate_epub_edition_date_current` run against the real tree, full history, clean. No EDITION_DATE value was changed: the constant was correct all along.

**Not a decision, a correction to this cycle's own record:** the 19:4x entry's "0 FAIL" claim should be read as "0 FAIL through the point it was pushed," not as the run's real final result, which arrived after. Naming this plainly rather than leaving a quietly-wrong "0 FAIL" sitting next to the truth, per CLAUDE.md 0.4.

Pushed to main: `ops/preflight.py`, `ops/tests/test_last_commit_epoch_shallow_boundary.py`, `ops/cycle-signal.json`, this entry.

## Scheduled operator cycle, 2026-11-03: the orphan-process-chain class named five times on 2026-11-02 alone, gated at its root instead of killed a sixth time

**Did.** Unshallowed and attached to main cleanly (621 then several more commits fast-forwarded across the session as concurrent cycles kept landing). All 30 open GitHub issues re-checked live: unchanged, all `decision`/`blocked-on-art`, #42 untouched. `BACKLOG-2026-09-07.md` sections 2-6: nothing unstruck except C5/C6, both Phil-gated. `room_guide_candidates.py` rerun fresh: same conclusion five concurrent cycles already reached today, Family Room (2 genuine rows, already tried and reverted once for a real scorer collision) and Mudroom (1, noise) both too thin for a guide. No mail credentials. Per CLAUDE.md 0.2/10b: a defect class named in five consecutive log entries today ("orphan-process chain from a preflight kill," `test_audit_catalog.py`'s own grandchild and `build_etsy_assets.py`'s Chrome render each surviving a kill of the top-level `preflight.py`) with no gate, is this cycle's actual highest-value work, not another kill-and-note.

**Root cause, checked directly rather than assumed.** `_run_bounded`'s own `start_new_session=True` (added 2026-09-30 so a 700s TimeoutExpired could `killpg` a whole grandchild tree) has a side effect nobody had traced: it also detaches that child from the top-level `preflight.py` process's own tree, so when an operator SIGKILLs `preflight.py` itself from the outside (the routine way every one of today's cycles ended a stalled run, well before its own internal bounds fired), the detached child is no longer reachable through the dead parent at all. It survives forever, nothing left holds its pgid. `acquire_preflight_lock`'s existing stale-holder detection (dead pid, zombie, recycled pid) already runs on every later cycle's own startup; it just never looked for this.

**Fixed at the root.** `_track_lock_child_pgid`/`_untrack_lock_child_pgid` record each `_run_bounded` child's pgid into the held lock directory itself (a plain file, written before `communicate()`, so it survives a SIGKILL of the parent). `_reap_lock_children`, called from the stale-lock branch right before the directory is removed, kills every pgid still listed and still alive. Added Half 5 to the existing self-test gate `gate_preflight_lock_blocks_concurrent_runs`: spawns a real session-leader subprocess, records it the same way `_run_bounded` does, marks its holder dead, and asserts the orphan is gone once the lock breaks.

**Verified.** Fail-then-pass proved directly: stashed the `_reap_lock_children` call, reran the gate function in isolation, watched the new case fail by name ("left its recorded child pgid ... running"); restored, reran clean. `python -c "import ast; ast.parse(...)"` parses; `fix_dashes.py --check` on the changed file: 0/0. A full `preflight.py --skip-tests` was started fresh and, this time, left running to its own completion rather than killed early (the thing none of today's five prior occurrences actually tried): it reached `gate_etsy_pdfs_current` and `gate_shop_prerendered`, both previously blamed for "stalling," and resolved both on nothing more than patience past the elapsed point earlier cycles had been killing them at, inside their own existing bounds. The full pass reached the end: **every gate passed, 37 warning(s)**, all previously-documented sandbox limits (no Stripe/SSH credential here, no local narrated-video build, known art gaps already tracked). `gate_tests` itself stayed skipped, named by its own WARN, not claimed passing.

**Went well:** traced a repeated symptom to its actual mechanism instead of killing it a sixth time; the fix is in the one place (the lock directory) that survives the exact failure mode it protects against.

**Did not go well:** the five prior cycles that hit this today each spent real time on manual `pkill`/`kill -9` bookkeeping that this fix now makes unnecessary; none of them had enough standing instruction to escalate from "clean up" to "stop cleaning up and fix it," until CLAUDE.md's own three-strikes rule applied.

**Changing next cycle:** when a kill-and-clean orphan description recurs a fourth time in `ops/NIGHTLY-LOG.md` for the *same* subprocess shape, stop logging it and check whether `_track_lock_child_pgid` already covers it; if a new subprocess spawner needs the same protection, wire it through `_run_bounded` rather than inventing a parallel mechanism.

**Next:** the structured queue is still exhausted beyond C5/C6 (Phil-gated); 30 GitHub issues await a reply. Real next lever is Phil's own decisions, not more autonomous cycles re-confirming the same state.

Pushed to main. `ops/preflight.py`, this entry. No content, price or product touched, no new page; IndexNow not applicable.

## Scheduled operator cycle, 2026-11-02 (09:1x slot): CI red fix, caught by actually watching the run instead of trusting the local preflight pass

The prior cycle's full local `preflight.py --skip-tests` run gave 0 FAIL on everything it reached, but that run skips the Python test suite and was run before this cycle's own merge with a concurrent PM check-in. Watched the resulting push's CI run (`41418638318`) to completion rather than assume green: it failed, 4 gates. Traced each directly rather than guessed from the gate name alone.

**Real cause, one root: a stale citation left behind after an edit, the same recurring class sections 64-79 have each found in a different document.** `site/feed.xml` still held the long (202-char) meta description for the new laundry room article from before that description was shortened to fix `audit_pages.py`'s `desc-long` gate; `build_feed.py` reads descriptions straight off the page, so the fix never propagated to the already-generated feed until rerun. `ROADMAP-2026-2029.md`'s "pages live" figure and `RISKS.md`'s `forms_dead` citation both still read 227 against the real, current 228 (the new article's own page), because both were written before the final page count was known rather than re-derived after.

**Fixed.** Reran `ops/build_feed.py` (confirmed the only diff was the one stale `<summary>` line). Updated both citations to 228, the number the running count in `ROADMAP-2026-2029.md`'s own "Then N on DATE" chain already ends at. Verified each of the three gate functions directly against the real files (`gate_feed_current`, `gate_roadmap_prices_current`, `gate_risks_evidence_current`): all three clean. Ran `ops/tests/test_gate_feed_current.py` and `ops/tests/test_gates.py` (the two test files CI's run also flagged): both OK.

**Went well.** Caught this by watching the actual CI conclusion rather than citing a local preflight pass that could not have caught it (the local run predated the merge, and `--skip-tests` does not run the file CI's full suite does). This is exactly the gap `CLAUDE.md` 0.3/0.4 names: a local pass is not production, and a run that could not look must say so, not stand in for a check that never happened.

**No new gate needed.** `gate_feed_current`, `gate_roadmap_prices_current` and `gate_risks_evidence_current` already existed and caught all three correctly; they simply had not been checked against the final committed state before this push, because the prior local preflight run predated the final edits.

Shipped via `ops/ship.py --no-deploy` (`f66c0df5e`), which only touches `site/`, so (correctly, by this workflow's own documented path-filter design) it did not retrigger `checks.yml` itself; `publish-image.yml` did fire automatically and was still `in_progress` as this entry was written. ## Addendum, 2026-11-01 (21:0x): the Checks run the 20:4x entry below left unchecked finished, green, end to end; the whole incident is closed

The 20:1x and 20:4x entries below are both mine, from the same continuous
session across two scheduled firings, not two different cycles disagreeing;
this closes the loop the 20:4x entry explicitly asked the next cycle to
check.

**Checks run `41348698433` (workflow_dispatch on `5fdeba19d`) finished at
21:02:28Z: `conclusion: success`.** Preflight step (20:48:57 to 20:57:24,
about 8.5 minutes, the normal duration), "The ops test suite" (20:57:24 to
21:02:17, success), "Product copy has not drifted" (success). Confirmed by
reading the job steps directly, not by trusting the green checkmark alone.

**Full incident, for whoever reads this cold.** The 19:4x operator's
workshop-article commit carried a real but tiny defect:
`ROADMAP-2026-2029.md`'s section 2 headline still read "226 pages live"
while the site had moved to 227; `gate_roadmap_prices_current` and
`test_gates.py` both correctly caught it, and the real `Checks` CI went red
on it (not just a local/sandbox artefact; confirmed via GitHub Actions job
logs). Fixed the one number (20:1x). That alone did not turn CI green: the
same bad commit had also failed `publish-image.yml`'s own build (same root
cause, since it runs preflight too), which left the live site's deployed
build behind HEAD and `gate_publish_image_current` failing for a different,
real reason. Manually re-dispatched `publish-image.yml`; it built and
published clean. The first `deploy.yml` run after that (auto-triggered on
the publish) restarted the production container but could not read it back
immediately afterward (`products live after: None`) and correctly refused
to claim success per its own "unchecked is not deployed" rule, rather than
a real outage: this sandbox has no egress to the live domain to check
directly, so re-dispatched `deploy.yml` a minute later and it confirmed
production current at build `52bc629000f31119`, matching HEAD, zero
commits undeployed (`deploy_gap_material_commits` re-derived directly,
empty list). Re-dispatched `checks.yml` itself to get an honest green
record rather than leave a stale red one on file, which is the run
confirmed green above.

**Learning worth keeping:** a fix to the root cause of a CI failure does
not retroactively clean the log of that failure, and a path-filtered
workflow (`publish-image.yml` only fires on `site/`/Dockerfile changes)
will not auto-retry just because the next commit happens to fix the gate
that broke it; both needed an explicit `workflow_dispatch` this cycle.
Worth a future cycle checking whether `gate_ci_conclusion_current` or a
sibling gate should itself suggest the re-dispatch when it detects this
exact shape (last run failed, no site-touching commit since) rather than
relying on whoever reads the warning to work that out by hand.

No further action needed; no notification sent (production was never
actually down, confirmed, and the gap closed within the same session that
found it). 30 open GitHub issues unchanged, all `decision`/`blocked-on-art`,
all Phil-gated.

## Same cycle, follow-up: the mobile touch-target thread A53 left open was a flake, not a defect. Closed.

The backgrounded `python ops/audit_visual.py --all --mobile` (230 pages) finished: **0 touch targets under 44px, 0 crowded under 24px, 0 pages scrolling sideways, sitewide.** It also surfaced the real mechanism: "fonts NOT loaded: 20 page(s) ... measured against a fallback face, so they are not what a visitor sees" on a handful of deck pages during that run. Reran the single page that had read 42-45 under-44px targets twice earlier (`site/zones/nursery-the-crib-and-sleep-zone.html`) a third time, in isolation again: it now reads 0. The same command, same page, same unmodified markup, three different counts (0, then 42, then 45, now 0 again) is not a real defect moving under me, it is a measurement race: a single-page, cold-browser invocation sometimes measures before the real webfont has finished loading, so nav links and heading text get measured against a fallback face with different metrics, exactly the "timing flake in the .reveal fade-in transition versus the probe's fixed 250ms settle time" `gate_mobile_touch_targets`'s own docstring already names as a known, filed-not-gated flake for contrast; this is the same class, one page-load race it had not yet named for touch targets specifically. The full `--all` run does not hit this race, or hits it rarely enough that this one run read clean. Not gated further this cycle: the existing gate already requires a real browser and already treats unparseable/partial output as `warn`, not pass, and a second flake class under the same already-documented mechanism does not need a second writeup, just this one closed honestly rather than left as an open question. The companion full `preflight.py` run (also backgrounded) was still inside its documented slow `gate_tests` stage when this entry was written, with 0 FAIL and only the two already-standing WARNs (dated disclosures, image-coverage build-asset gap) in everything before it; not re-cited further here since the real open question, the mobile touch-target claim, is independently settled by the two runs above regardless of how `gate_tests` resolves.

No code, content or gate changed this entry; this is a correction to this cycle's own earlier open thread, not a new defect or fix.

## Addendum to the A52 cycle below: the full `preflight.py` run it backgrounded was genuinely hung, not slow, settled by the background harness's own 30-minute kill

The A52 entry below left a full `preflight.py` run going in the background,
stalled at `gate_tests`, and reported it honestly as unchecked rather than
assumed passing. That run has now been settled, not left open: the
background harness's own 30-minute limit killed it with CPU time still flat
and no further output after `...gate_tests`, the same line it had been
sitting on since shortly after it started. No exit code was ever written,
because the process was killed externally rather than exiting.

This is the clean version of the standing "hang vs. slow" question several
recent entries have gone back and forth on: a run that makes zero CPU
progress for a full 30 minutes, not just past the usual ~180s foreground
timeout, is a genuine hang on this cycle's sandbox, not the "just slow,
finishes in ~9.5 minutes if left alone" shape one earlier addendum
described from a single clean finish. Both are real; which one happens
appears to depend on the sandbox instance, not on the code. Worth the next
cycle that re-litigates this noting both outcomes exist rather than treating
either as settled.

No new gate added: `gate_tests` sits last in `preflight.py`'s own gate
order specifically so every other gate still gets a real answer before it,
and `cycle_signal.py`'s checkpoint (built for exactly this problem) already
lets a later cycle skip re-running the full suite when nothing has changed
since a clean pass. This cycle's A52 content change is independently
verified clean by the narrower checks the A52 entry already lists; nothing
about this unresolved `gate_tests` run calls that into question.

## PM check-in, 2026-10-29 18:4x slot (continued): the CI run this cycle's own earlier entry was waiting on came back red, for a real reason, fixed

NEXT FOR THE OPERATOR: watch the GitHub Actions run for commit 80f52eab5 (this fix) to confirm green; if `gate_tests` fails again for an unrelated reason, that is real work, not the exhausted-backlog state.

The 18:45 entry below handed off "watch run 40932546417 for green." It finished red: `gate_tests` actually completed end to end this time (6m10s in CI, `test_gate_keyword_demand_global_rescored_current.py` the one real failure out of 454 files), rather than hanging the way it usually does, so this is new signal, not the usual unchecked timeout. Read the job log directly via the GitHub API rather than trust the one-line summary.

**Root cause, found by reading the actual script, not just the gate:** `ops/keyword_demand_global.py`'s plain harvest path (`main()`, no `--rescore`) scores every query against the live `site/` corpus at harvest time, exactly like `--rescore` does, but never stamped `scored_against_commit` on the payload it writes; only the `--rescore`/`rescore()` path did. So every weekly scheduled harvest silently dropped the field the staleness gate depends on, and the file stayed in a permanent "never checked" WARN state until someone happened to run `--rescore` by hand afterward. `ops/keyword_demand.py`, the US sibling, has the identical bug in its own plain-harvest payload construction; it only wasn't failing today because its committed file still carried a `scored_against_commit` from a manual rescore after the last harvest, a coincidence of timing, not a difference in correctness.

**Fixed at the source, both files:** added `"scored_against_commit": head_commit()` (`kd.head_commit()` for the global file) to the payload dict each plain harvest already builds, mirroring what `rescore()` already does, since both paths score against the same corpus at the same moment. Re-ran `python ops/keyword_demand_global.py --rescore` (free, no network) once to stamp the already-committed file that was missing the field, rather than leave it broken until next week's scheduled harvest. Verified: `test_gate_keyword_demand_global_rescored_current.py` and its US sibling `test_gate_keyword_demand_rescored_current.py` both pass; `test_keyword_demand.py`, `test_gate_keyword_demand_global_not_stale.py`, `test_gate_goals_keyword_cluster_citation_current.py`, `test_gate_also_called_is_heading.py`, `test_room_also_called.py` all still pass, no regression. A full local `gate_tests` re-run (all 454 files) was started in the background to cover the rest of the suite before shipping further; its result, if anything new turned up, is recorded separately.

Checking what that kill actually left behind found the real story: the killed process's own grandchild, `test_audit_catalog.py`'s own `audit_catalog.py --include-fixtures` subprocess (pid 738), survived the kill as an orphan (reparented to pid 1) and kept running, because `kill -9` on the parent reaches only the parent, never a grandchild it spawned, exactly the failure mode `_run_bounded()`'s own 2026-09-30 docstring already names and guards against **when preflight's own internal timeout does the killing**. **Started a second, fresh `preflight.py` run and did not touch it this time.** Backgrounded, checked on periodically without killing anything, across roughly 100 minutes of wall time in this session's own current load (425 of 450 `ops/tests/test_*.py` files done by minute 70, all 450 by around minute 100). ## 2026-10-28, PM check-in (18:4x slot): red checks.yml found and fixed, root cause was a one-line stale citation, not a real defect

NEXT FOR THE OPERATOR: watch the next checks.yml run on this push (or fire one), because this entry's fix is the only thing standing between the current red run and a clean one, and confirming it go green clears gate_ci_conclusion_current for every cycle after it.

**Previous work finished, but checks.yml was quietly red since 18:11Z and nobody had looked.** Attached clean: the unshallow fetch ran long, so this entry waited for it rather than trusting a shallow-graft read; checkout main, merge --ff-only onto origin/main, no reset. `cycle_signal.py --check`: SAME. `preflight.py --fast` backgrounded: reached its 115s budget with `cycle_signal: not recorded, this run has failing gate(s)` before gate_tests, a message no cycle today had produced. That line only means a FAIL is pending somewhere in the gates already run; the per-gate FAIL text itself only prints in the final summary, which this sandbox's gate_tests hang always prevents reaching, so a real failing gate can sit invisible behind "0 FAIL through every gate reached" unless it is checked for directly, which no cycle today had done.

**Traced it rather than guessing.** Monkeypatched `preflight.fail()` to print immediately (scratch script, nothing committed) and re-ran: `gate_ci_conclusion_current` fired locally, confirming checks.yml's own run 40739718057 (commit `d84d51ddd2`, the 17:4x operator cycle) concluded `failure`, live from the Actions API, not cited. Pulled that job's own log directly: the "Preflight" step failed in CI (CI does not hang on gate_tests the way this sandbox does, so it ran the gates after it too) on `FAIL risks-evidence-current RISKS.md cites a stale ops/state.json value: 'forms_dead=218' cited, ops/state.json has forms_dead=219`. 1 gate failed, 35 warnings, all the same standing sandbox-credential gaps every cycle already logs.

**Root cause, not a defect.** `ops/state.json`'s `forms_dead` moved 218 to 219 (commit `5457193ba`) when today's new `/articles/how-to-store-blankets` page (Phil's own commit) added one more page carrying the same inert footer form as every other page, exactly the "nothing new in kind" shape RISKS.md's own RISK-0012 history already names and already has precedent for (commit touching this exact same citation, 217 to 218, logged the same way). Its own house rule: enumerate a new history line only when the addition is different in kind; otherwise update the headline count and nothing else. Fixed by that rule: `RISK-0012`'s evidence line now reads `forms_dead=219`. Verified against the real gate function, not a rewrite of its logic: imported `ops/preflight.py`, cleared `FAIL`, called `gate_risks_evidence_current()` directly, `FAIL == []`. `fix_dashes.py --check`: clean. Diff is one line.

**Went well:** checking for a failing gate hidden behind the gate_tests hang instead of accepting "0 FAIL through every gate reached" at face value, the exact theatre CLAUDE.md 0.4 warns about; tracing to the real root cause in the CI log instead of only re-stating the symptom.

**Did not go well:** this is at least the second time this exact citation has gone stale and been caught after a red build rather than before one (same shape, 217 to 218, logged earlier in RISKS.md's own history); the file's existing rule already prevents a new history line each time, but nothing yet prevents the headline number itself from going stale between page-adding commits. Worth a cheap fix for a future cycle: have whatever regenerates `ops/state.json`'s `forms_dead` also patch this one RISKS.md line automatically, the same way other generator-owned fields are kept current, rather than relying on a gate to catch it after the fact.

Before writing that down as a new defect, checked the actual cause: `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` was still `true` even after STEP 0's unshallow step ran, because that fetch hit a mid-transfer TLS disconnect (`GnuTLS recv error`) that left a stale `.git/shallow.lock`, so the later unconditional `git fetch --unshallow` silently no-opped. With the clone stuck shallow at a 61-commit synthetic root, `git log -1 -- path` for any file last really touched before that boundary returns the boundary commit's own date, which is today, manufacturing 271 false "last touched 2026-10-23" readings out of a sandbox limitation, exactly the trap CLAUDE.md 0.4 warns against (unchecked must not report as passing, and the same logic cuts the other way: a measurement tool's own blind spot must not get written down as a code defect either). Retried the unshallow until the stale lock cleared; repo is now a real 8,336-commit history, not shallow. Re-ran the ledger: 1 genuinely stale entry (`ops/check_cron_cadence.py`, touched by this hour's own CI fix, not yet re-ledgered), which is correct and expected, not a defect.

GitHub: 10 open issues re-pulled fresh, unchanged, all `decision`/`blocked-on-art`; issue #42 (the cadence-re-verifying-exhaustion decision) carries no new comment since 2026-10-23T00:21Z. 0 open PRs.

## 2026-10-22, scheduled operator cycle: cold-read of ops/build_product_images.py found and fixed a real, reproduced-live pagination bug

**Did:** Attached clean (fetch, unshallow, checkout -B main origin/main,
ff-only, 407 commits fast-forwarded in, tree clean). Read BACKLOG-2026-09-07.md
sections 0-7 (all Done/Closed/Hold/Phil-gated), ROADMAP-2026-2029.md and the
last 4 log entries, which all pointed at the same handoff:
`ops/cold_read_ledger.py --next` names `ops/build_product_images.py` (369
lines, un-ledgered). Ran `preflight.py` in the background first; it took far
longer than the usual documented stall point but was genuinely progressing
(changing child processes throughout, not flat CPU), so let it run to
completion instead of killing it: 0 FAIL on the clean tree, 29 standing
warnings, all previously diagnosed sandbox-access limits (no Stripe
credential, no network, no SSH key, no mail credential).

Read `ops/build_product_images.py` in full. `manual_spread()` crops a
hardcoded page (22) out of a fresh browser-print of the Manual's own HTML for
`product-manual.jpg`'s sample. Reproduced live rather than suspected: printing
the same committed source in this sandbox put the intended "Lower Cabinet and
Cookware Zone" heading on page 20, not 22; page 22 held an unrelated zone's
cleaning table with no zone name on it. Chromium's print-to-PDF pagination
depends on font metrics and is not portable across machines, so a hardcoded
index is fragile by construction. The shipped image (built elsewhere) was
correct; nothing would have caught a future `--force` regeneration shipping
the wrong zone, since the only gate tied to this generator checks file
existence, not content.

**Verified:** Fixed at the root with a new `find_page(pdf, needle)` that
locates a page by its own heading text; `manual_spread()` now uses it for
both crops it takes. Regenerated `product-manual.jpg` with the fix in this
same sandbox: lands on page 20, shows the correct zone and all six passes.
New `ops/tests/test_build_product_images.py`, fail-then-pass proved directly
(`git stash` reproduces an `AttributeError` without the fix; clean with it
restored). Regenerated the image's 420/840 jpg/webp variants and the two
avif siblings `write()` correctly invalidated (`ops/build_avif.py --encode`).
`gate_product_images_exist`, `check_urls.py` (213/213), `fix_dashes.py
--check` (0/0), `affiliate.py --check` (165 documents) all clean after.
Ledgered as fixed in `ops/cold-read-ledger.json`. No mail credential here
(`inbox_agent.py --apply`: unchecked, not empty); 10 open GitHub issues read
directly, unchanged, all `decision`/`blocked-on-art`, none from Phil, 0 PRs.
No price or product touched; one existing product-tile image corrected in
place.

With that lane clean, picked up `OWNER-ACTIONS.md`'s own open "worth checking before discarding" question instead of starting a new cold-read sweep: whether `photos/server.py` actually carries the two security fixes (negative Content-Length, socket timeout) from Phil's unpushed 2026-10-14 local commit, which a 2026-10-21 cycle had guessed "most likely yes" without reading the file. Read `photos/server.py` directly: neither fix was present. `_body()` parsed `Content-Length` with a bare `int()`, so a negative value skips the `n > limit` check and reaches `self.rfile.read(n)` with `n < 0`, which blocks until the connection closes rather than reading a bounded amount; `Handler.timeout` was left at `BaseHTTPRequestHandler`'s default `None`, so an idle connection holds a `ThreadingHTTPServer` thread forever. Fixed both: a guard rejecting `n < 0` (and an unparseable value) in `_body()`, and `Handler.timeout = PHOTOS_SOCKET_TIMEOUT` (env-configurable, default 30s).

**Verified.** Proved fail-then-pass directly, not assumed: reverted both fixes, reran `ops/tests/test_photos_service.py`, and the new `negative-content-length-refused` case failed exactly as the finding describes (the request hung until the test's own client closed the connection, then the server raised the wrong error against an already-gone peer, logged as a broken pipe); restored the fix, 39/39 clean. While verifying, found a third, smaller gap: the disk-free floor (`shutil.disk_usage`, from the 2026-10-15 review pass) had real, correctly-placed code but no test anywhere, despite `PHOTOS-API.md` claiming "every fix above is proved fail-then-pass." Added that test too (monkeypatching `shutil.disk_usage`); disabling the real check in `store.py` and rerunning confirmed the new case is what catches it (40/40 with the floor live). `store.py` itself needed no code change, only the missing test. `cold_read_ledger.py` updated (`photos/server.py` now `fixed`, dated and noted); `PHOTOS-API.md`'s security-review section and `OWNER-ACTIONS.md`'s own item rewritten to state the verified fact in place of the guess, narrowing what remains to Phil to the `site/photos.html`-vs-`site/photo-check.html` product call alone.
